entries.claim: Payment for physical-product orders is processed via Stripe or PayPal, after which the order appears in the dashboard to be prepared and shipped.
entries.verbatim: ## Questions fréquentes sur la vente des produits physiques sur systeme.io Comment vendre des produits physiques avec systeme.io ? Créez une fiche produit dans votre compte systeme.io depuis la section Produits. Ajoutez vos images, définissez le prix, configurez les variantes comme la taille ou la couleur, puis ajoutez vos frais de livraison. Ensuite, ajoutez le produit à une étape de tunnel ou à une page de site avec un bouton d’achat. Lorsqu’un client achète, il est redirigé vers la page de paiement. Le paiement est traité via Stripe ou PayPal, puis la commande apparaît dans votre tableau de bord pour être préparée et expédiée. Vous pouvez aussi ajouter des upsells et des séquences email après achat depuis la même plateforme.

entries.claim: systeme.io is positioned as ideal for creators selling merchandise, physical books, or a small range of products alongside their digital products.
entries.verbatim: systeme.io fonctionne-t-il comme une plateforme e-commerce pour les produits physiques ? Oui, surtout pour les business qui vendent une gamme limitée de produits physiques via des tunnels. Systeme.io permet de créer des fiches produits, gérer les variantes, suivre les stocks, calculer les frais de livraison, gérer les commandes et encaisser les paiements. C’est idéal pour les créateurs qui vendent des produits dérivés, des livres physiques ou une petite gamme de produits en complément de leurs produits numériques. En revanche, systeme.io n’est pas conçu pour les grandes boutiques e-commerce qui ont besoin d’une gestion de catalogue avancée, d’intégrations logistiques complexes ou d’outils de stock très poussés comme Shopify ou WooCommerce.

entries.claim: Shopify starts at $39/month and charges 2% on third-party payment processors.
entries.verbatim: systeme.io est-il meilleur que Shopify ou WooCommerce pour vendre des produits physiques ? Pour la plupart des créateurs qui vendent aussi une gamme de produits physiques, systeme.io est plus simple et moins cher. Vous obtenez une plateforme marketing complète avec emails, tunnels, automatisations et vente de produits physiques, le tout avec 0 % de frais de transaction. Shopify commence à 39 $/mois et facture 2 % sur les processeurs tiers. WooCommerce nécessite un hébergement, de la maintenance de plugins et des outils marketing supplémentaires. Le compromis : Shopify et WooCommerce offrent des outils de stock et de logistique beaucoup plus avancés pour les business centrés principalement sur la vente physique.

entries.claim: There is not yet an automatic product import tool, so migrating an existing physical-product store requires manually recreating product listings in systeme.io.
entries.verbatim: Comment migrer ma boutique de produits physiques existante vers systeme.io ? Exportez votre liste de produits et vos données clients depuis votre plateforme actuelle au format CSV. Importez vos contacts dans systeme.io depuis la section Contacts. Recréez ensuite vos fiches produits manuellement dans systeme.io, car il n’existe pas encore d’outil d’import automatique des produits. Configurez vos règles de livraison, puis connectez Stripe ou PayPal. Enfin, mettez à jour les liens externes qui pointaient vers votre ancienne boutique pour les rediriger vers votre nouveau tunnel ou site systeme.io. L’équipe de migration systeme.io peut vous aider dans ce processus après votre inscription au plan Illimité ou à un plan annuel.

voice.tone: Direct and benefit-first: it names the pain point (a separate Shopify or WooCommerce store, hidden fees) and immediately removes it with a concrete number or mechanism. No hype adjectives, no exclamation points — the confidence comes from specifics (SKU generation, real-time stock, 50 tunnels) rather than enthusiasm.
voice.rhythm: Explanatory paragraphs of two to three sentences: the first states the capability, the next unpacks how it works mechanically, and a clause set off by em-dash or bold often lands the key reassurance or number at the end.
voice.person: Speaks as the product by its own name — 'systeme.io vous permet...' — not as 'nous' or 'je'; the reader is addressed directly as 'vous'.
exemplars: systeme.io vous permet de vendre des produits physiques **directement via vos tunnels et votre site web** — sans avoir besoin d’une boutique Shopify ou WooCommerce séparée. Vous pouvez créer des fiches produits avec images, descriptions et variantes (taille, couleur, matière), avec génération automatique des SKU et suivi des stocks en temps réel. Les frais de livraison sont calculés automatiquement selon le poids de la commande, son montant ou la localisation du client, et **systeme.io ne prélève aucun frais de transaction sur tous les plans**.

Avec systeme.io, chaque plan vous permet de créer un nombre illimité de sous-comptes. Chaque sous-compte est un compte systeme.io à part avec ses propres limites Les limites pour chaque sous-compte sont les mêmes que celles du plan de votre compte principal, sans frais supplémentaires. Par exemple : si votre plan permet 50 tunnels, chaque sous-compte que vous créez peut également avoir 50 tunnels

segments.name: A corporate trainer launching a paid course while holding a website, an email tool and a third-party course platform together by hand
segments.situation: She teaches for a living and has decided the next step is a course she sells herself. The site is in one place, the list is in another, and the course content sits on a third-party tool she has to embed and connect — a customer in systeme.io's own testimonials describes exactly that setup: "un site web d'un côté, le marketing par email de l'autre, et en essayant d'intégrer un créateur de formations tiers". Each launch means re-checking that a buyer actually lands on the right tags, the right sequence and the right lesson access, because nothing hands off to anything else on its own. She has already looked at the specialist platforms: another systeme.io customer records being "sur le point de m'inscrire chez AWeber" and comparing Kajabi before choosing. objections.objection: "All-in-one means mediocre at everything. My specialist course platform and my specialist email tool each do one job properly — this will do nine jobs badly, and I'll find out after I've moved."
objections.answer: The strongest honest answer is scope, not superlatives. Every feature is available on every plan including the free one, with paid plans only raising limits (E71), and the feature list is specific rather than vague: courses with video, PDF downloads, drip content, module locking and student progress tracking (E48, E73); funnels with templates, A/B tests, upsells, order bumps and countdowns (E39); automation on a trigger-condition-action model that connects purchase to course enrolment to welcome email to CRM stage with no Zapier (E50, E74, E75); funnel signups flowing straight into the list, tagged and sequenced, with no external integration (E72). It also helps that the vendor names where it is genuinely weaker — it states plainly that it is not built for large stores needing advanced catalogue management or logistics, and concedes Shopify and WooCommerce are far better there (E27, E32). One customer who compared Kajabi concluded systeme.io had as much to offer (E80), but that is one person's judgement, not a benchmark. Nothing in the evidence compares feature depth against Kajabi, ActiveCampaign or Teachable independently, so the copy should argue "one integrated chain" and not "as good as each specialist".

provenance.quote: J'ai également examiné les similitudes entre Kajabi et systeme.io. Ma conclusion est que vous avez tout autant à offrir.

objections.objection: "Switching is the real price. Rebuilding every funnel, moving the list, redirecting links and re-uploading a course is a week I don't have, and I'll be mid-migration when a launch lands."
objections.answer: Partially answerable, and the gaps must be named rather than smoothed. Free migration is offered (E90) and the migration team will help — but only after signing up to the Illimité plan or an annual plan (E34), which is a paid commitment made before the work is proven. For a physical-products store the documentation is explicit that there is no automatic product import yet and listings must be recreated by hand, with contacts imported by CSV, shipping rules reconfigured, Stripe or PayPal reconnected and external links repointed (E33). The free plan lets her build and test everything before paying or cutting over (E78), which is the honest de-risking move: run the new chain in parallel, switch when it works. Nothing in the evidence states how long a migration takes, what the team actually does, or whether funnels and courses import automatically — do not imply it is effortless.

objections.objection: "The free plan is bait. I can't see what the paid plans cost, so I'll build my whole business on €0 and then be told the price once my list, my funnels and my students are inside."
objections.answer: The structure of the offer answers this better than any price can, because the supplied material contains no plan names and no plan prices at all — that is a real hole and the copy must not invent one. What is documented: entry is €0 (E36), the free account is described as free for life (E115), signup needs no credit card (E88, E116), the free plan carries 2,000 contacts, unlimited emails and a first funnel (E38), paid plans add no features and only raise limits such as contacts, funnels and courses (E71), annual billing gives two months free (E89), and transaction fees are 0% on all plans (E15) with no extra charge on payment processors (E94). So the price risk is a limit ceiling, not a feature paywall — and she can see exactly which limit she will hit before she pays. If a reader asks "how much is the next tier", nothing here answers it; send them to the pricing page rather than guess.

objections.objection: "Putting my site, my list, my checkout, my course and my client data inside one vendor I'd never heard of last month is a single point of failure. If they go down or go away, my business goes with them."
objections.answer: Only partly answerable. On the trust side: systeme.io states more than 500,000 entrepreneurs use it (E37, E83, E114), the founder states he has been selling courses since 2010 and built this out of dissatisfaction with existing stacks (E13), support runs seven days a week with a stated average response under two hours (E6, E7, E97, E96), email support is stated as 24/7 (E101), the help centre has step-by-step video tutorials for every feature (E79), and a 1-on-1 onboarding coaching session is listed (E102, though which plans include it is not specified). On the part that actually worries her — uptime, SLA, data portability, what happens to her contacts and course files if she leaves — the evidence says nothing. The only documented export path runs the other way, into systeme.io (E33). Treat the concentration risk as unanswered; the user-count figure is vendor-stated with no methodology (E114) and should not be used as proof of reliability.

objections.objection: "This is a beginners' tool. It's cheap because it's for people making their first funnel, and I'll outgrow it inside a year."
objections.answer: The evidence cuts both ways and the copy should not pretend otherwise. systeme.io itself says the platform is designed for beginners and requires no technical skill (E76), and the customer testimonial most likely to be read as endorsement actually caps the ceiling — Alex calls it the best solution "pour les spécialistes du marketing en ligne débutants ou intermédiaires" (E81). Against that: the documented capability set is not beginner-only — CRM pipelines with Kanban stages and automation triggers on deal movement (E62), evergreen webinars with scheduled replays and reminders (E64), unlimited sub-accounts each with full plan limits at no extra cost (E98, E99), white label on a custom domain keeping 100% of revenue with no transaction fees (E68), A/B testing, upsells and order bumps (E39), SMS on the same automation engine as email (E60). The one documented hard ceiling is physical-product scale: advanced catalogue management, complex logistics and deep inventory tooling are explicitly out of scope (E27, E32). Say where the ceiling is instead of denying there is one.

provenance.quote: C'est actuellement la meilleure solution pour les spécialistes du marketing en ligne débutants ou intermédiaires sur le marché.

objections.objection: "I already have this. My site is on WordPress, my list is on Mailchimp, and I've just paid a year up front. Even if yours is better, this is the wrong month."
objections.answer: The sunk annual cost is not answered anywhere in the evidence — no trial extension, no credit, no refund or guarantee appears in the material (guarantees: none found), so timing stays a real objection. What can be argued is the ongoing cost of keeping the stack: WooCommerce needs hosting, plugin maintenance and extra marketing tools on top (E31, vendor's own comparison, not independent), automations across systeme.io's features need no Zapier or external automation tool (E50, E75), funnel-to-email handoff needs no integration (E72), and basic shipping rules need no external shipping app (E29). Practically, the free plan with 2,000 contacts, unlimited emails and a first funnel and no credit card (E38, E88) lets her rebuild one funnel alongside what she has and switch at renewal rather than mid-term. Do not claim savings figures: the "dix fois moins cher" line is an unattributed vendor paraphrase of customer feedback with no comparison target (E8) and should not be used as a price claim.

objections.objection: "Unlimited emails on a free plan means a shared-IP sending reputation. If my deliverability drops, I lose the list I spent three years building — that costs me more than any subscription."
objections.answer: Nothing in the supplied evidence answers this. Unlimited sending on all plans is documented (E41, E91) and the free plan includes 2,000 contacts (E38), but there is no statement anywhere about deliverability, sending reputation, dedicated IPs, authentication, inbox rates or any email performance measurement. This objection cannot be beaten with what we currently know; any deliverability reassurance in copy would be invented. Either raise it and point to the free plan as a way to test sending with her own list before migrating (E78), or stay off the subject entirely.

objections.objection: "My clients' data cannot sit in my personal account, and if I'm charged per client this stops being profitable at client number four."
objections.answer: This one is answered cleanly. Every plan allows an unlimited number of sub-accounts, each a separate systeme.io account with its own limits (E98), and those limits match the main plan's at no extra charge — if the plan allows 50 funnels, each sub-account can also have 50 (E99, where the 50 figure is the vendor's illustrative example, not a stated limit). Sub-accounts are explicitly built for agencies and consultants managing multiple clients, each a fully independent space with its own funnels, contacts, emails and courses (E56). For the branding half of the objection, white label puts the platform on her own domain in a space entirely under her brand, keeping 100% of revenue with no transaction fees (E68), positioned against GoHighLevel, ActiveCampaign and Vendasta (E69, vendor's own comparison). What is not documented: which plans include white label, or any client-permission or access-control detail inside a sub-account.

objections.objection: "I'll sign up free, get overwhelmed by eleven modules I didn't ask for, and never publish anything — like the last three tools I registered for."
objections.answer: Documented and reasonably well covered: the editor is drag-and-drop with ready-made templates for funnels, pages and courses (E77, E39), a complete multi-page site with a blog and custom domain is claimed in under 10 minutes and is included even on the free plan with no hosting, plugins or technical setup (E43, E44), physical products drop into any order form or sales page as an element with no code (E21), the help centre carries step-by-step video tutorials for every feature (E79), a 1-on-1 onboarding coaching session is listed (E102), and support answers seven days a week with a stated average response under two hours (E97). The 10-minute claim is the vendor's own capability statement, not a measured onboarding result — attribute it, don't promise it.

objections.objection: "I sell physical products too. A marketing platform bolting on a store will fall over the first time I have variants, stock and shipping rules to handle — and then I'm running two systems anyway."
objections.answer: Documented in unusual detail for a small catalogue: physical products sell directly through funnels and the website with no separate Shopify or WooCommerce store (E14), variants across size, colour and material with automatic SKU generation (E16, E28), real-time stock tracking to avoid overselling (E17), shipping as a flat rate or calculated by weight, order amount or customer location with delivery zones and carrier rates (E18, E22, E28), all configured in the product settings with no external shipping app for basic rules (E29), orders filterable by date, status or product (E20, E23), payment via Stripe or PayPal with the order landing in the dashboard to prepare and ship (E24), 0% transaction fees on all plans (E15), plus upsells and post-purchase email from the same platform (E25). The honest limit, stated by systeme.io itself: not built for large stores needing advanced catalogue management, complex logistics integrations or deep inventory tooling, where Shopify and WooCommerce are better (E27, E32). If her catalogue is a few products beside a digital offer, this holds; if physical sales are the business, it does not.

profiles.discovery_reason: The email tool a solo entrepreneur is likely already paying for and has to decide whether to fold into systeme.io or keep running alongside it.
profiles.one_liner: Transformez vos idées en e-mails & SMS qui créent du lien
profiles.promise: That Mailchimp's AI (Intuit Intelligence) will mine your own customer data to surface your next growth opportunity — such as which lapsed customers to win back — making data-driven, AI-assisted email and SMS marketing the engine for business growth.
profiles.pricing: Usage-tiered paid plans (Standard, Premium) priced by contact-count tier and capped monthly email volume (e.g. Standard: 'Envoyez jusqu'à 6 000 e-mails chaque mois'; Premium: 'Envoyez jusqu'à 150 000 e-mails chaque mois'); promotional intro pricing of 15% off for 12 months and 15% off for 10,000+ contacts is shown alongside the regular ('à partir de') rate; larger contact volumes require contacting sales for custom pricing.
profiles.free_entry: 14-day free trial of the Standard (or Essentials) monthly plan — requires valid payment information at signup, limited to new customers or existing free-plan customers with an account created in the last 90 days in certain countries; can downgrade anytime to the free plan.
profiles.icp: Segmented on their own site by: e-commerce ('E‑MAILS ET SMS POUR L'E‑COMMERCE'), small businesses ('POUR LES PETITES ENTREPRISES'), nonprofits/community organizations ('POUR LES ORGANISATIONS À BUT NON LUCRATIF'), professional services firms ('POUR LES PROFESSIONNELS'), and content creators ('MARKETING PAR E‑MAIL POUR LES CRÉATEURS DE CONTENU').

map.validation_note: Product requirements rechecked against current Knowledge in one closed-world call. Audience identities and market evidence are retained; market sources were not refetched.
map.reading:
Assessment summary. Verified quotations do not establish demand or purchase intent; commercial priority remains a hypothesis.
- An independent author selling books and companion products direct while building an owned reader list: review first; product compatibility supported; audience evidence supported (7 quoted source(s)); use or purchase unknown; reachability venue identified.
- A corporate trainer launching a paid course while holding a website, an email tool and a third-party course platform together by hand: hypothesis; product compatibility supported; audience evidence absent (1 quoted source(s)); use or purchase unknown; reachability unknown.
- A solo creator — photographer, coach, freelancer — paying monthly for a stack of apps that costs more than the side of the business it supports: hypothesis; product compatibility supported; audience evidence absent (2 quoted source(s)); use or purchase unknown; reachability unknown.
- A freelance marketing consultant running funnels and lists for a handful of clients out of one tangled set of logins: hypothesis; product compatibility supported; audience evidence absent (2 quoted source(s)); use or purchase unknown; reachability unknown.

situation.text: Independent author-publishers with established catalogs are adding or planning owned storefronts so they can sell books, signed editions, bundles, and related products directly to readers while maintaining a direct reader relationship.

evidence.quote: As an independent author-publisher, keeping my catalog organized and straightforward matters.
I’ve set up various book bundles of my series, so there is a New York Friendship Bundle, a New York Spark Starter Set and the Ultimate Book Bundle (see below).

situation.inference_basis: This combines observed direct-selling practices from three individual authors; it does not establish that all independent authors follow this model.

incumbent_behaviour.text: One author tested simple payment links through a newsletter and social media before building a Shopify store for signed books.

evidence.quote: It started with an experiment. I created simple payment links where you could buy signed copies directly from me, and then shared those links in my newsletter and on social media.

incumbent_behaviour.text: Another author initially connected Shopify to Bookvault for print-on-demand shipping, then moved website-order distribution and fulfilment into her own warehouse.

evidence.quote: So I integrated with Bookvault and stayed with POD shipping until February 2025. Since February 2025, I’ve been distributing and fulfilling all orders from my website in my own warehouse.

incumbent_behaviour.text: One author uses separate Shopify and StoryOrigin storefronts for US and international sales and offers ebook bundles plus US-only paperbacks.

evidence.quote: I actually had to create two stores–KathyStrobosBooks.com (for US) (a Shopify store) and a books.kathystrobos.com site (for everyone) (StoryOrigin).
You can also buy paperbacks from me directly (in the US only).

incumbent_behaviour.text: Author newsletters commonly support release announcements and list growth through back-matter and social links, according to BookBub's survey respondents.

evidence.quote: The vast majority of authors (92%) use email to update their readers on new books, and 70% do this in the form of cover reveals.

evidence.quote: Yes I’m an author, but running your own fulfillment from website sales means you also run an eCommerce business.

problems.statement: Major retail and social platforms can leave authors without a direct reader relationship and expose their reach to platform-controlled algorithms or traffic dependence.

evidence.quote: Whether you’re checking Gmail, scrolling TikTok, or browsing Amazon, algorithms decide what you see, and those algorithms are designed to maximally benefit their respective platform at everyone else’s expense.
But I didn’t want to be beholden to TikTok the way I’d been beholdened to other sources of income and I knew if I’d gone viral once, I could do it again and that would lead to relying on TikTok.

problems.statement: At the self-fulfilment end of direct selling, warehousing, staffing, paperwork, shipping, and problem resolution create substantial operational work that can reduce time available for publishing.

evidence.quote: I recognise that this model is not for 99% of authors. It’s a LOT of work. It’s a lot of logistics, a lot of peopling, team building, paperwork and problem solving. This is as far removed from sitting behind a desk and writing 24/7 as you can get.
I usually write and publish 3 books a year and this year I’ve dropped to 2 published.
Problems arise in all areas of this business, from shipping to label printing to packaging to import and export paperwork, to sourcing products, VAT, pricing, website, delivery issues.

review_notes: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

problems.statement: Physical-book preorders create inventory and scheduling risk: too little stock can leave orders uncovered, while excess stock consumes cash and space.

evidence.quote: Under ordering stock is a terrifying prospect. As is over ordering because do you have enough space for it and what if you then don’t sell it?
a solid 20% of the order arrived damaged by rain. But we’d already sold almost all the initial print run so we couldn’t spare 20% and thus didn’t have enough stock to cover our preorders.

review_notes: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

problems.statement: Self-fulfilled launches require coordination across writing deadlines, print delivery, staff availability, product ordering, preparation, and fulfilment periods; failures can force the author to stop writing and fulfil orders personally.

evidence.quote: The second mistake was releasing a book without checking the diaries of the warehouse team who happened to be on holiday during the fulfillment process.
Meaning I had to stop writing and fulfill 1000 preorders single handedly.
So we’ve produced a heat map style document with everyone’s leave, delivery dates, deadlines for me, product ordering dates, prepping dates and fulfillment periods etc.

review_notes: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

dossier.orientation: For an independent author-publisher building an owned reader list while selling a limited range of books and companion products directly, systeme.io is an all-in-one platform for funnels, email marketing, physical-product sales, payments, stock, shipping rules, and order handling.

ranked_relevance.why: Funnels, email marketing, automation, and physical products in one platform directly match the audience's defining direct-sales and reader-list workflow.
Direct physical-product sales through an author's funnels and website support moving transactions onto an author-controlled storefront.
Post-purchase email sequences on the same platform provide a documented mechanism for communicating with direct buyers after purchase.
Real-time stock tracking directly addresses the overselling portion of the audience's documented inventory risk.
Filtering orders by date, status, or product supports the preparation and shipping workflow implicated in fulfilment workload and launch coordination.
The no-code physical-product element documents how authors can place images, prices, and descriptions on order forms or sales pages.
Variant and automatic SKU management is relevant to limited catalogues containing different editions, formats, colours, or companion-product variants.
Delivery zones, carrier rates, and automatic fee rules support basic shipping administration within the direct-sales workflow.
Basic shipping rules can be configured in product settings without an external shipping app, but the evidence expressly limits this to basic rules.
The documented Stripe-or-PayPal checkout-to-dashboard flow explains how paid physical-product orders enter preparation and shipping.
This documented exception is essential because systeme.io is not designed for stores requiring advanced catalogues, complex logistics integrations, or very advanced inventory tools.
Migration-team help is relevant to authors leaving an existing storefront, subject to enrollment in the Illimité plan or an annual plan.
A free-for-life account may reduce trial friction, but the audience research establishes no acquisition-cost problem and this excerpt does not specify plan limits.
The Shopify price comparison is vendor-supplied, dated April 2026, and does not address the audience's defining need or measured costs.
The ten-times-cheaper statement has no specified comparison target or supporting calculation.
A photographer's consolidation experience does not establish an outcome for an independent author's direct-sales workflow.
A corporate trainer's opinion about combining tools is less relevant than the documented mechanisms and does not prove an author outcome.
The vague customer superlative names no comparison basis and offers no evidence about direct book sales or fulfilment.
Affiliate-program management is documented, but the audience research does not establish an affiliate workflow.
Cash on delivery is documented, but the audience research does not establish this payment requirement.
The vendor identifies creators selling physical books or a small physical range alongside digital products as a target segment, but this is weak positioning language rather than functional proof.
The vendor concedes that Shopify and WooCommerce provide more advanced inventory and logistics tools for businesses primarily focused on physical sales.

problem_fits.caveat: Automatic capture of buyers as consented email contacts, data ownership, portability, and reduced algorithm dependence are not established by the selected evidence.
problem_fits.why: The platform supports direct storefront sales, email marketing, and post-purchase sequences, but the evidence does not prove the complete owned-reader-relationship outcome.

problem_fits.caveat: Warehouse staffing, label printing, packaging, VAT, import/export paperwork, delivery-problem resolution, and complex logistics integrations are not supported; E27 expressly limits suitability for advanced logistics.
problem_fits.why: Stock tracking, order filters, and basic shipping rules address administrative portions of fulfilment but not the audience's broader operational burden.

problem_fits.caveat: Demand forecasting, print-run purchasing, damaged inventory, storage capacity, and cash tied up in excess stock are not established by the selected evidence.
problem_fits.why: Real-time stock tracking can reduce overselling, but it does not solve the preorder procurement and scheduling risks described by the audience.

problem_fits.caveat: Staff availability, writing and print deadlines, product-ordering dates, preparation calendars, and fulfilment capacity planning are not established by the selected evidence.
problem_fits.why: Order filtering helps identify what must ship and when, but does not establish the cross-team launch-coordination workflow the problem requires.

evidence.quote: ## Questions fréquentes sur la vente des produits physiques sur systeme.io Comment vendre des produits physiques avec systeme.io ? Créez une fiche produit dans votre compte systeme.io depuis la section Produits. Ajoutez vos images, définissez le prix, configurez les variantes comme la taille ou la couleur, puis ajoutez vos frais de livraison. Ensuite, ajoutez le produit à une étape de tunnel ou à une page de site avec un bouton d’achat. Lorsqu’un client achète, il est redirigé vers la page de paiement. Le paiement est traité via Stripe ou PayPal, puis la commande apparaît dans votre tableau de bord pour être préparée et expédiée. Vous pouvez aussi ajouter des upsells et des séquences email après achat depuis la même plateforme.

research.audience_name: An independent author selling books and companion products direct while building an owned reader list

required_structural_signals.description: Author controls marketing decisions for their own catalogue or small imprint.

required_workflow_signals.description: Maintains or is actively building an email list of readers.
Sells or plans to sell books, bundles, downloads or companion education directly.

optional_signals.description: Has several published titles that can support repeat direct campaigns.
Ships a limited range of signed editions or bundles.

hard_disqualifiers.description: Requires advanced warehouse, tax or print-on-demand integrations not established in supplied capabilities.
Has no intent to capture reader data or sell directly.

eligible_subsegments: Nonfiction experts selling books and courses
excluded_subsegments: Authors committed exclusively to retailer distribution

situation.text: Independent author-publishers with established catalogs are adding or planning owned storefronts so they can sell books, signed editions, bundles, and related products directly to readers while maintaining a direct reader relationship.

evidence.quote: As an independent author-publisher, keeping my catalog organized and straightforward matters.
I’ve set up various book bundles of my series, so there is a New York Friendship Bundle, a New York Spark Starter Set and the Ultimate Book Bundle (see below).

situation.inference_basis: This combines observed direct-selling practices from three individual authors; it does not establish that all independent authors follow this model.

incumbent_behaviour.text: One author tested simple payment links through a newsletter and social media before building a Shopify store for signed books.

evidence.quote: It started with an experiment. I created simple payment links where you could buy signed copies directly from me, and then shared those links in my newsletter and on social media.

incumbent_behaviour.text: Another author initially connected Shopify to Bookvault for print-on-demand shipping, then moved website-order distribution and fulfilment into her own warehouse.

evidence.quote: So I integrated with Bookvault and stayed with POD shipping until February 2025. Since February 2025, I’ve been distributing and fulfilling all orders from my website in my own warehouse.

incumbent_behaviour.text: One author uses separate Shopify and StoryOrigin storefronts for US and international sales and offers ebook bundles plus US-only paperbacks.

evidence.quote: I actually had to create two stores–KathyStrobosBooks.com (for US) (a Shopify store) and a books.kathystrobos.com site (for everyone) (StoryOrigin).
You can also buy paperbacks from me directly (in the US only).

incumbent_behaviour.inference_basis: Historical sources (2024-03-06); present applicability is not corroborated.

incumbent_behaviour.text: Author newsletters commonly support release announcements and list growth through back-matter and social links, according to BookBub's survey respondents.

evidence.quote: The vast majority of authors (92%) use email to update their readers on new books, and 70% do this in the form of cover reveals.

incumbent_behaviour.inference_basis: This is third-party survey reporting from more than 500 respondents, not direct testimony from a specific buyer in the corpus.; Historical sources (2023-04-27); present applicability is not corroborated.

sophistication_basis.text: The observed audience members understand direct commerce as a distinct operating model and name specific storefront, digital-delivery, printing, shipping, and fulfilment solutions.

evidence.quote: Yes I’m an author, but running your own fulfillment from website sales means you also run an eCommerce business.

problems.statement: Major retail and social platforms can leave authors without a direct reader relationship and expose their reach to platform-controlled algorithms or traffic dependence.

evidence.quote: Whether you’re checking Gmail, scrolling TikTok, or browsing Amazon, algorithms decide what you see, and those algorithms are designed to maximally benefit their respective platform at everyone else’s expense.
But I didn’t want to be beholden to TikTok the way I’d been beholdened to other sources of income and I knew if I’d gone viral once, I could do it again and that would lead to relying on TikTok.

problems.statement: At the self-fulfilment end of direct selling, warehousing, staffing, paperwork, shipping, and problem resolution create substantial operational work that can reduce time available for publishing.

evidence.quote: I recognise that this model is not for 99% of authors. It’s a LOT of work. It’s a lot of logistics, a lot of peopling, team building, paperwork and problem solving. This is as far removed from sitting behind a desk and writing 24/7 as you can get.
I usually write and publish 3 books a year and this year I’ve dropped to 2 published.
Problems arise in all areas of this business, from shipping to label printing to packaging to import and export paperwork, to sourcing products, VAT, pricing, website, delivery issues.

review_notes: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

problems.statement: Physical-book preorders create inventory and scheduling risk: too little stock can leave orders uncovered, while excess stock consumes cash and space.

evidence.quote: Under ordering stock is a terrifying prospect. As is over ordering because do you have enough space for it and what if you then don’t sell it?
a solid 20% of the order arrived damaged by rain. But we’d already sold almost all the initial print run so we couldn’t spare 20% and thus didn’t have enough stock to cover our preorders.

review_notes: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

problems.statement: Self-fulfilled launches require coordination across writing deadlines, print delivery, staff availability, product ordering, preparation, and fulfilment periods; failures can force the author to stop writing and fulfil orders personally.

evidence.quote: The second mistake was releasing a book without checking the diaries of the warehouse team who happened to be on holiday during the fulfillment process.
Meaning I had to stop writing and fulfill 1000 preorders single handedly.
So we’ve produced a heat map style document with everyone’s leave, delivery dates, deadlines for me, product ordering dates, prepping dates and fulfillment periods etc.

review_notes: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

ranked_relevance.why: Funnels, email marketing, automation, and physical products in one platform directly match the audience's defining direct-sales and reader-list workflow.
Direct physical-product sales through an author's funnels and website support moving transactions onto an author-controlled storefront.
Post-purchase email sequences on the same platform provide a documented mechanism for communicating with direct buyers after purchase.
Real-time stock tracking directly addresses the overselling portion of the audience's documented inventory risk.
Filtering orders by date, status, or product supports the preparation and shipping workflow implicated in fulfilment workload and launch coordination.
The no-code physical-product element documents how authors can place images, prices, and descriptions on order forms or sales pages.
Variant and automatic SKU management is relevant to limited catalogues containing different editions, formats, colours, or companion-product variants.
Delivery zones, carrier rates, and automatic fee rules support basic shipping administration within the direct-sales workflow.
Basic shipping rules can be configured in product settings without an external shipping app, but the evidence expressly limits this to basic rules.
The documented Stripe-or-PayPal checkout-to-dashboard flow explains how paid physical-product orders enter preparation and shipping.
This documented exception is essential because systeme.io is not designed for stores requiring advanced catalogues, complex logistics integrations, or very advanced inventory tools.
Migration-team help is relevant to authors leaving an existing storefront, subject to enrollment in the Illimité plan or an annual plan.
A free-for-life account may reduce trial friction, but the audience research establishes no acquisition-cost problem and this excerpt does not specify plan limits.
The Shopify price comparison is vendor-supplied, dated April 2026, and does not address the audience's defining need or measured costs.
The ten-times-cheaper statement has no specified comparison target or supporting calculation.
A photographer's consolidation experience does not establish an outcome for an independent author's direct-sales workflow.
A corporate trainer's opinion about combining tools is less relevant than the documented mechanisms and does not prove an author outcome.
The vague customer superlative names no comparison basis and offers no evidence about direct book sales or fulfilment.
Affiliate-program management is documented, but the audience research does not establish an affiliate workflow.
Cash on delivery is documented, but the audience research does not establish this payment requirement.
The vendor identifies creators selling physical books or a small physical range alongside digital products as a target segment, but this is weak positioning language rather than functional proof.
The vendor concedes that Shopify and WooCommerce provide more advanced inventory and logistics tools for businesses primarily focused on physical sales.
